question: Will the official result of the Lamag by-election (Sabah), scheduled for January 24, 2026, be overturned before May 1, 2026?
summary: Objections reveal a non-zero overturn risk due to ongoing Sabah election petitions (Sindumin and related filings).
Lamag's large margin (5,681) reduces overturn likelihood but does not eliminate the possibility, as historical precedents show overturns can occur in Malaysia/Sabah in rare cases.
There is no publicly reported Lamag-specific petition as of early 2026, but Sabah's petition activity keeps a non-zero risk by May 1, 2026.
Disposition timelines (six months) could yield a ruling within the relevant window, though timing remains uncertain.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections identify valid non-zero overturn risk from petitions and precedents, but the large Lamag margin and absence of Lamag-specific petitions reduce the probability meaningfully.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.02 to 0.05 to reflect non-zero Sabah-specific petition risk; no downward adjustment given implausible scenarios are not needed.

forecasts.reference-class: Sabah/Malaysia election petitions and court challenges to electoral results (by-elections and parliamentary seats), including Sabah's Kimanis 2018 overturn and Sindumin petition filed in 2025, used as the base-rate reference for potential overturns in Sabah.

Asian Electoral Resource Center overview: Malaysia allows election petitions; outlines dispute-resolution processes and timeframes.
Election Commission must wait until the appeal period ends in an election petition case before taking the next step.

The Star reports that, in GE15, some wins were upheld in court, indicating that not all petitions overturn results and outcomes can remain unchanged.

([theborneopost.com](https://www.theborneopost.com/2025/12/26/sabah-polls-election-petition-filed-after-video-shows-alleged-ballot-misconduct-in-sindumin/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent of Sabah overturns (Kimanis 2018)
causal-factors.rationale: Kimanis 2018 demonstrates that Sabah results have been overturned in the past, indicating that electoral challenges can succeed under certain conditions. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2018/11/19/kimanis-parliamentry-seat-belongs-to-anifah-says-election-court/1695054?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Judicial disposition timeline for election petitions (six-month disposal window)
causal-factors.rationale: There is a potential six-month disposition window for election petitions, which could constrain or accelerate rulings and limit protracted delays, reducing long-lead overturn risk by May 1, 2026. ([theedgemalaysia.com](https://theedgemalaysia.com/article/cj-all-election-petitions-will-be-disposed-6-months?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: The baseline 2% overturn risk is modestly uplifted to about 5% to account for Sabah petition activity and rare overturn cases, while the large Lamag margin and lack of Lamag-specific petitions keep overturn risk low overall. The likelihood of an overturn before May 1, 2026 remains unlikely, but non-zero.
